podcasts.name: A History of Rock Music in 500 Songs

podcast.title: Admired by Cornel Gunter
podcast.body: Cornel Gunter, a member of The Coasters, greatly admired singer Dinah Washington and frequently performed imitations of her during the group's shows. "Gunter had always admired the singer Diner Washington, and he used to do imitations of her in the group shows."

srcs.source: A History of Rock Music in 500 Songs

podcast.title: Childhood Singing Partner
podcast.body: Jazz singer Billy Paul performed with the acclaimed Dinah Washington during his childhood, marking his early exposure and immersion in the jazz genre. "This was a guy who sang with the great Dino Washington when he was a child"

srcs.episode: Ep. 37 - Philly Soul and the Sound of the 70s

podcast.title: Hired and Fired Cornel Gunter
podcast.body: Cornel Gunter left The Coasters to join Dinah Washington's backing group. However, Gunter was soon sacked by Washington, which led him to form his own version of The Coasters. "Shortly after its release Cornel Gunter decided to leave the group and take up an opportunity to sing in Diana Washington's backing group."

srcs.source: A History of Rock Music in 500 Songs

podcast.title: Inspired Gunter's Performance on "One by One"
podcast.body: Cornell Gunter's imitation of Dinah Washington's style was highlighted as he shone on three solo lead songs on The Coasters' "One by One" album. "Gunter had always admired the singer Diner Washington, and he used to do imitations of her in the group shows."

srcs.source: A History of Rock Music in 500 Songs

podcast.title: Songs Closer to Jazz than Country
podcast.body: Dinah Washington's songs, along with those of Ruth Brown and LeVern Baker, were described as having a sound closer to jazz than to country music, a quality that Janice Martin embraced in her repertoire with country instrumentation. "The songs, Brown, Baker and Washington recorded were all closer to jazz than to country music."

srcs.source: A History of Rock Music in 500 Songs
